description: qou-cds1 branch 3, two owner-directed questions, both negative. (1) Riera-Rodriguez Theorem 2 decoded by DERIVATION rather than by a clean scan: given j(tau_0) = -25/2 the possible j(5 tau_0) are the six roots of Phi_5(-25/2,Y), computed here, and -3810.78125 = -5*29^3/2^5 = -121945/32 is among them, matching the garbled OCR '- 293x5' with its 2^5 exponent on the next line. Both invariants are NON-INTEGRAL rationals (v_2 = -1 and -5), i.e. potentially multiplicative reduction at 2, which CM forbids -- so tau_0 is NOT a CM point and the hypothesis that it might be where Serre's E is not is REFUTED. (2) The Grobner-Shirshov jet tower is BLIND to the decay channel: the q-Plancherel weight depends on a partition only through its hook multiset, which transpose permutes, and transpose swaps the trivial and sign branchings, so w_sym(k) = w_alt(k) exactly at every k and every q (verified: zero counterexamples to hook invariance for k <= 9; |w_sym - w_alt| <= 7.3e-40 at 40 dps). Mass sees y_3 + y_(1^3) and decay sees y_3 - y_(1^3), so the tower contributes IDENTICALLY ZERO to decay -- no phase can hide there. Lean: BringEllipticCurveJInvariant.lean and JetTowerBlindToDecay.lean, sorry-free.

assertions.name: j_five_tau_zero_is_minus_5_times_29_cubed_over_32
assertions.detail: -5*29^3/2^5 = -121945/32 appears among the six roots of Phi_5(-25/2,Y) as j((tau+2)/5), decoding the OCR fragment '- 293x5' with its '2^5' exponent OCR'd onto the next line — derived, with the scan only selecting

assertions.name: neither_theorem_2_invariant_is_integral
assertions.detail: v_2 = -1 and -5; a CM j-invariant is an algebraic integer, so negative 2-adic valuation (potentially multiplicative reduction, Tate curves) rules CM out

assertions.name: tau_zero_is_not_a_CM_point
assertions.detail: the owner's hypothesis — that tau_0, a period-matrix parameter, might be CM where Serre's isogeny factor is not — is REFUTED. tau_0 has no closed form and supplies no derived phase

assertions.name: hook_multiset_is_transpose_invariant
assertions.detail: zero counterexamples over every partition of every k <= 9, so the q-Plancherel weight W_lambda = [k]_q!/(prod [h]_q)^2 satisfies W_lambda' = W_lambda for every q

assertions.name: jet_tower_sym_and_alt_weights_are_equal
assertions.detail: worst |w_sym - w_alt| over k=3..9 is 7.34684e-40 at 40 dps (exactly 0 for k=3,4,5) — the equality is exact, the residue is roundoff

assertions.name: jet_tower_contributes_nothing_to_the_decay_channel
assertions.detail: mass sees y_3 + y_(1^3), decay sees y_3 - y_(1^3); w_sym - w_alt = 0 identically at every level, so no phase can hide in the tower (Lean decay_combination_zero)

parameters.source: library/pjm-v154-n1-p09-s — Riera & Rodriguez, The period matrix of Bring's curve, Pacific J. Math. 154 (1992) 179-200
parameters.lean_vs_numeric: LEAN: the two j-values as rational identities, their non-integrality, and the involution reindexing that makes the tower blind. NUMERIC: that -3810.78125 is among the six Phi_5 roots; hook-multiset transpose invariance (standard, checked exhaustively k<=9, not formalised); w_sym = w_alt at 40 dps.

context.axis: branch 3: is tau_0 CM? can the jet tower hide the phase?
context.answer: No and no. tau_0's two j-invariants are non-integral rationals (Tate curves at 2), so no CM and no closed form. The jet tower's sym and alt weights are exactly equal at every level by hook-multiset transpose invariance, so its contribution to the decay combination y_3 - y_(1^3) vanishes identically -- it contributes nothing to the channel that needs a phase.
context.consequence: branch 3 is out of NAMED candidates: the braid image is excluded, arbitrary M is circular, constant-residue holonomies fail the doubling identity, all real-spectrum generators are on the wrong side of 1, Im(q) cannot supply ellipticity, Bring's E is non-CM, tau_0 is non-CM, and the jet tower is blind. What remains is unnamed.
context.scope: Scope-(b) for both exclusions. Nothing derived, proposed, wired or readmitted; no convention adjudicated.
